series.premise: In the mountain kingdom of Veyra, thirteen-year-old apprentice clockmaker Anya discovers that the moon is an ancient machine—and every night someone is stealing one minute from it.
series.season_engine: Each stolen minute creates a physical time-fault in Veyra; repairing it reveals who built the Moon Engine, why Anya can hear its gears, and what the royal family erased from history.
series.ending_promise: Anya must repair time without restoring the unjust system the Moon Engine was designed to protect.
series.global_image_style: Vertical 9:16 premium cute cinematic 3D feature-animation, original compact stylized characters with large expressive eyes, tactile brass clockwork, moon-silver magic and jewel-toned mountain environments, warm candlelight against cool lunar glow, coherent anatomy and props, emotionally truthful acting, adventurous rather than violent; preserve all locked character sheets exactly.

characters.name: Anya Vale
characters.lock: small brown-skinned mountain girl, huge dark amber eyes, round freckled face, thick black hair in one messy side braid tied with copper wire, teal wool coat over cream shirt, burgundy tool apron, brown leggings, brass-toed boots, crescent-shaped hearing lens over left ear
characters.acting: listens before acting; courage appears as careful hands becoming steady

characters.name: Pip
characters.role: fox-shaped automaton and lost Moon Engine key
characters.lock: tiny brass-and-ivory clockwork fox, cyan glass eyes, one copper ear and one silver ear, segmented tail with seven plates, visible heart gear behind round chest window
characters.acting: precise fox movement; emotion through ear angle, tail rhythm and heart-gear speed

characters.name: Rian Sol
characters.role: fourteen-year-old runaway prince and sky-map reader
characters.lock: slender brown-skinned boy, large grey-green eyes, soft black curls, midnight-blue short cape with gold star stitching, white high-collar shirt, charcoal trousers, worn red climbing boots, broken crown pin used as compass
characters.acting: trained politeness cracks into dry humor; steps between danger and others before admitting fear

characters.name: Master Mara Vale
characters.role: Anya's grandmother, royal clockmaker and keeper of a dangerous secret
characters.lock: short elderly brown-skinned woman, sharp warm eyes, silver hair in a braided bun, plum mechanic robe, leather tool belt, round magnifying spectacles, left hand made of elegant brass fingers
characters.acting: love expressed through teaching and preparation, never helpless sentiment

characters.name: Selene
characters.role: ageless child custodian of the Moon Engine
characters.lock: small moon-pale girl, luminous violet eyes, waist-length white hair floating as if underwater, layered silver-blue robe with gear-shaped hems, bare feet leaving tiny constellations
characters.acting: ancient patience inside childlike stillness; wonder returns slowly

characters.name: Regent Vale
characters.role: Anya's estranged father and ruler preserving the stolen timeline
characters.lock: tall brown-skinned man early forties, severe amber eyes matching Anya, straight black hair streaked silver at temples, black-and-gold royal coat with mechanical shoulder mantle, moonstone signet glove
characters.acting: controlled and persuasive; fear of losing Anya leaks through only in his hands

characters.name: Orlo
characters.role: giant clockbird who carries the moon's counterweight
characters.lock: large friendly owl-like clockwork bird, layered bronze feathers, round moon-white eyes, cobalt enamel wing tips, hanging silver counterweight beneath chest
characters.acting: majestic weight with gentle curiosity; wing beats always feel mechanical and powerful

characters.name: Queen Elara
characters.role: Anya's missing mother and the last human Moon Winder
characters.lock: brown-skinned woman late thirties, luminous amber eyes, very long black braid threaded with moon-silver wire, ivory-and-cobalt mechanic gown, brass forearm guards, crescent scar across right palm
characters.acting: exhausted physical discipline with immediate maternal warmth; never behaves like a mystical prize

episodes.title: The Moon Lost a Minute
episodes.logline: Anya hears the moon skip and finds one impossible silver gear in her workshop.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya confirms that time is physically breaking and awakens Pip.
episodes.location: Vale clock shop beneath the moonlit bell tower
beats: At midnight, every clock in Veyra jumps from 12:08 to 12:10 while Anya alone hears a gear scream above the clouds.
A moon-silver cog crashes through the clock-shop roof without leaving a hole in the tiles.
Master Mara orders Anya never to touch royal metal, but hides fear behind an ordinary repair lesson.
Anya fits the cog into a broken brass fox she has repaired since childhood.
The fox wakes, bows once, and projects a map of gears turning inside the moon.
A black tooth is missing from the projected Moon Engine, exactly the shape of the stolen minute.
Anya names the fox Pip and promises Mara she will only study him inside the shop.
Pip steals Anya's hearing lens and races toward the forbidden bell tower as midnight strikes twice.

episodes.title: Midnight Struck Twice
episodes.logline: A duplicated midnight traps the market in a repeating disaster.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya learns Pip can enter small time-faults and chooses to repair them publicly.
episodes.location: Veyra night market frozen between two midnights
beats: The market repeats the same falling lantern every sixty seconds while everyone forgets each loop.
Anya marks her wrist with soot so she can prove the repetition to herself.
Pip slips between two frozen raindrops and reveals a black gear tooth inside the bell's shadow.
Mara arrives with royal guards behind her and tells Anya to leave the fault untouched.
Anya sees a fruit seller's child trapped beneath the lantern in every loop.
She uses Pip's tail as a temporary escapement, slowing the repeated minute enough to move the child.
The market remembers all its loops at once, and the rescued people see Anya holding lunar machinery.
A runaway boy wearing a broken crown pin whispers that the Regent has been collecting the missing teeth.

episodes.title: The Prince Stole Her Map
episodes.logline: Rian steals Pip's moon map to expose his father's hidden gear vault.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Rian joins Anya after revealing the palace hoards stolen minutes.
episodes.location: rooftops between the market and Moon Palace
beats: The runaway grabs Pip, leaps onto a cable tram, and apologizes with perfect royal manners.
Anya pursues across wet copper rooftops while Pip deliberately drops tail plates as a trail.
The thief introduces himself as Prince Rian, missing from palace portraits for six months.
He says Regent Vale locked away every recovered moon gear instead of repairing the sky.
Anya does not trust a prince who begins with theft, even when his evidence matches Pip's map.
Rian returns Pip and lets Anya decide whether to follow him into the palace ventilation clock.
She chooses the dangerous proof over Mara's unexplained prohibition.
Inside the palace wall, they hear Anya's own father ordering a new minute removed before dawn.

episodes.title: Her Father Ordered the Theft
episodes.logline: Anya discovers Regent Vale is her father and watches him steal a minute to save a village.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya learns the theft prevents an avalanche but accelerates the Moon Engine's failure.
episodes.location: palace lunar control chamber
beats: Through a brass vent, Anya sees Regent Vale wearing the same amber eyes and crescent birthmark she sees in mirrors.
Rian admits the Regent is Anya's father and that Mara hid her after the queen vanished.
Vale extracts a black gear tooth from moonlight and inserts it into a mountain model.
Time stops around a distant village just before an avalanche can bury it.
Anya realizes the stolen minute saves real lives, making the theft harder to condemn.
Pip's heart gear overheats because every removed minute shifts the moon's counterweight.
Anya records the mechanism with her hearing lens instead of confronting Vale unprepared.
Vale looks directly at the vent and says, welcome home, daughter.

episodes.title: The Regent Offered Her Tomorrow
episodes.logline: Vale offers Anya a future without disasters if she helps him steal more time.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya rejects Vale's private bargain and loses access to the palace.
episodes.location: Regent Vale's mechanical observatory
beats: Vale receives Anya without guards and shows a clockwork model predicting every storm, illness and accident.
He says each stolen minute can freeze one tragedy long enough for rescuers to intervene.
The model displays a future where Mara survives an approaching heart failure.
Rian argues that the frozen villages never move forward and have become invisible prisons.
Vale offers Anya the royal clockmaker seal if she repairs the extraction machine.
Anya refuses to save people by deciding alone which minutes they must lose.
She returns the moon gear, but Pip bites through the extraction lever before they flee.
Vale seals every city gate and announces that Anya stole the kingdom's tomorrow.

episodes.title: The City Hunted Its Clockmaker
episodes.logline: Branded a thief, Anya must repair a time-fault without letting frightened citizens identify her.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Ordinary citizens begin secretly helping Anya repair time.
episodes.location: canal district during a royal manhunt
beats: Mechanical posters unfold across the canal district showing Anya's silhouette without readable words.
A fault makes a ferry cross the same broken bridge again and again, closer to falling each loop.
Rian urges escape while Anya insists the passengers cannot wait for her reputation to recover.
Disguised under laundry cloth, she reaches the bridge's clock housing as guards search below.
Pip finds the stolen minute embedded in the ferryman's repeated decision to turn left.
Anya repairs the choice rather than the clock, allowing the ferryman to see the danger and stop.
The passengers recognize her but misdirect the guards with nine different escape stories.
An elderly passenger gives Anya a forbidden moon-key once carried by her missing mother.

episodes.title: Her Mother Left a Door in Time
episodes.logline: The moon-key opens a workshop belonging to Anya's vanished mother.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya finds proof that Queen Elara entered the Moon Engine willingly.
episodes.location: hidden workshop inside an unmoving waterfall
beats: The moon-key stops one ribbon of waterfall, revealing a dry door behind the rushing water.
Inside, clocks built by Queen Elara tick backward toward Anya's birth.
Mara admits Elara was both queen and the last human Moon Winder.
A recorded mechanical tableau shows Elara climbing a silver ladder into the moon during a famine.
Vale told the kingdom she died, but her final clock still receives a heartbeat each midnight.
Anya wants to follow immediately; Mara insists the ladder opens only after all stolen minutes return.
They find a ledger showing Vale removed the first minute on the night Elara disappeared.
Elara's heartbeat clock stops, then taps Anya's name in repair code.

episodes.title: The Moon Called Her Name
episodes.logline: A message from inside the moon sends Anya toward the sleeping clockbird Orlo.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya locates Orlo, the only creature capable of reaching the Moon Engine.
episodes.location: abandoned sky-dock above Veyra
beats: Elara's clock taps coordinates ending at a sky-dock closed since the queen vanished.
Thousands of bronze feathers cover a shape mistaken for a collapsed airship.
Pip inserts his silver ear into a socket and wakes the giant clockbird Orlo.
Orlo panics because his missing counterweight makes every wingbeat jump several seconds.
Rian climbs onto the bird to cut a rusted restraint while Anya matches her heartbeat to Orlo's escapement.
Mara surrenders her brass hand as a temporary counterweight, knowing it may never return.
Orlo rises steadily and reveals a ladder of moonlight above the clouds.
Royal harpoons strike the dock, and Vale orders Orlo captured before Anya can fly.

episodes.title: The Clockbird Chose the Ground
episodes.logline: Orlo refuses to abandon endangered workers, forcing Anya to choose rescue over reaching the moon.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Orlo freely joins Anya after she proves he is not merely transport.
episodes.location: collapsing royal sky-dock
beats: Harpoons tear the dock supports and send workers sliding toward the cloud edge.
Anya orders Orlo upward, but the bird folds his wings and shields the workers instead.
Rian reveals royal handlers treated Orlo as a machine that could not choose.
The moon ladder begins fading, perhaps their only chance to reach Elara.
Anya removes Orlo's command bridle even though doing so ends her authority over him.
Freed, Orlo catches the falling workers with both wings before the dock breaks.
He then kneels to Anya by choice, allowing Pip to restore his temporary counterweight.
The rescued foreman reveals Vale moved all stolen minutes into the bell tower for tonight's eclipse.

episodes.title: The Eclipse Needed Thirteen Minutes
episodes.logline: Vale attempts a thirteen-minute freeze that could stop every disaster—and stop the kingdom forever.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya breaks the mass freeze, but the Moon Engine falls out of alignment.
episodes.location: Veyra bell tower during total eclipse
beats: Thirteen black gear teeth orbit the bell as the eclipse turns Veyra silver-black.
Vale says freezing the kingdom tonight will protect it until the Moon Engine can be controlled.
Whole streets stop mid-motion while Anya and Pip move through tiny gaps between ticks.
Mara confronts Vale as his mother, admitting she taught him that protection excuses secrecy.
Rian frees the bell counterweight while Orlo carries Anya above the frozen mechanism.
Anya returns twelve minutes but keeps one tooth long enough to release every trapped village together.
The kingdom moves again and remembers the years stolen from it.
Above them, the moon's inner rings grind sideways and begin descending toward Veyra.

episodes.title: The Moon Began to Fall
episodes.logline: With the engine misaligned, falling lunar debris forces enemies into a temporary alliance.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya and Vale agree to cooperate under public rules.
episodes.location: Veyra central square beneath the descending moon rings
beats: Silver stones drift upward from rooftops as the moon's gravity reaches into the city.
Vale's guards cannot control the crowds now remembering their stolen years.
Anya demands that every repair decision be announced publicly before she helps him.
Vale accepts because a falling lunar ring will strike the mountain by dawn.
Pip projects three repair routes, each requiring a different neighborhood to lose time.
Rian proposes a fourth route: ask every district to donate one voluntary second.
The citizens agree after hearing the true cost and the moon ring stabilizes briefly.
Their donated seconds open a hidden kingdom between ticks where Selene waits alone.

episodes.title: The Girl Between Seconds
episodes.logline: Selene claims the moon was built as a prison, not a clock.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Selene enters Veyra and exposes the engine's original purpose.
episodes.location: silent silver garden between two seconds
beats: Anya, Pip and Rian step into a garden where falling petals never reach the ground.
Selene has waited there unchanged since the first Moon Winder abandoned her.
She says the Moon Engine regulates time only because it imprisons an ancient creature called the Dawn.
Every stolen minute weakened the cage and strengthened the creature's waking dream.
Anya doubts a custodian who knew about Veyra's suffering but never intervened.
Selene admits she cannot leave without another person freely taking her place.
Pip opens the garden gate from outside its rules, proving he is the missing mobile key.
Selene follows them into time, and sunrise appears beneath the mountains instead of above.

episodes.title: Sunrise Came From Below
episodes.logline: The waking Dawn turns shadows into possible futures that attack their owners.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Dawn gains a visible influence over Veyra.
episodes.location: inverted sunrise across the lower mountain streets
beats: Golden light pours upward from sewer grates and throws everyone's shadow into the sky.
Each shadow acts out the future its owner fears most, spreading panic faster than fire.
Anya's shadow becomes a cold royal clockmaker who values repairs above people.
Vale's shadow shows him alone in a perfectly safe frozen kingdom.
Selene explains the Dawn feeds on futures people try hardest to prevent.
Anya stops fighting her shadow and names the fear truthfully in front of the crowd.
The shadow returns to her feet, teaching citizens how to reclaim their own.
Rian's shadow refuses to return and climbs toward the palace wearing a complete crown.

episodes.title: The Prince's Shadow Took the Crown
episodes.logline: Rian's feared future seizes the palace and offers the city efficient rule without uncertainty.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Rian renounces inherited authority and earns public trust.
episodes.location: Moon Palace throne mechanism
beats: Shadow Rian locks the palace and makes every royal clock obey one flawless schedule.
Food arrives, guards respond, and frightened citizens begin praising a ruler who never hesitates.
Real Rian admits part of him wants the easy respect his shadow receives.
Anya refuses to defeat the shadow for him because the crown represents his choice.
Rian enters the throne mechanism unarmed and publicly lists every privilege the palace hid.
He breaks his crown pin and gives the compass half to a market council.
Without inherited authority to imitate, Shadow Rian collapses into ordinary shade.
The broken crown reveals a star map pointing to Elara's prison inside the Moon Engine.

episodes.title: The Queen Was Turning the Moon
episodes.logline: Anya reaches Elara but discovers her mother cannot stop winding without killing Selene.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya meets Elara and learns the human cost of the Moon Engine.
episodes.location: Moon Engine winding chamber
beats: Orlo carries the group through an opening in the lowest lunar ring.
Inside, colossal gears move because a lone woman walks an endless circular bridge.
Elara recognizes Anya by the repair rhythm she tapped as a baby.
Stopping the bridge would release the Dawn through Selene's heart, which serves as the final lock.
Selene knew the truth but hid it because she feared being treated as a component again.
Anya refuses Elara's request to replace her, rejecting another inherited sacrifice.
Pip finds empty sockets for seven mobile keys like himself around the chamber.
One socket activates and shows Vale secretly carrying the second clockwork animal.

episodes.title: Vale Built Another Pip
episodes.logline: Vale's hidden raven automaton offers a faster repair at the cost of Pip's identity.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Pip learns he is one of eight autonomous keys, not a unique tool.
episodes.location: Regent's sealed automaton aviary
beats: Vale opens an aviary where a sleek black clockwork raven hangs unfinished.
The raven contains copied pieces of Pip's heart gear and can stabilize two moon sockets.
Completing it requires melting Pip's silver ear and erasing his earliest memories.
Pip initially presents the sacrifice as the most efficient solution.
Anya asks whether efficiency is what Pip wants or only what makers taught him to say.
Pip chooses to help the raven wake without surrendering himself, accepting a slower repair.
The raven opens its eyes and identifies six other keys scattered across impossible time-faults.
Its first independent act is to fly away from Vale and warn that one key serves the Dawn.

episodes.title: The Key That Served the Dawn
episodes.logline: A serpent key sabotages the repairs because freedom for the Dawn means freedom for all constructs.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group recognizes the enemy key, Coil, as a political opponent rather than a monster.
episodes.location: glass desert created by a century-long noon
beats: The search leads to a desert where one stolen minute has stretched into a hundred-year noon.
A silver clockwork serpent named Coil has built a community of abandoned machines there.
Coil says the Moon Engine enslaved every key to maintain a human kingdom.
Pip cannot deny that his own instincts still pull him toward empty sockets.
Anya offers Coil freedom without requiring loyalty, but asks him not to erase Veyra's people.
Coil refuses because no prisoner should preserve a prison for its wardens.
Selene reveals she is both prisoner and living door, complicating Coil's certainty.
Coil steals the raven's core and gives the Dawn its first complete minute.

episodes.title: One Minute Became a Century
episodes.logline: Anya enters the stretched minute and returns older in memory but unchanged in body.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya gains a century of repair knowledge and rejects its emotional detachment.
episodes.location: glass desert's century-minute workshop
beats: To recover the stolen core, Anya crosses the boundary where sixty seconds contain a century.
She spends decades in a workshop studying the Moon Engine while her friends remain frozen outside.
Anya masters every gear but gradually refers to people as timing variables.
A tiny unchanged Pip repeatedly asks what she is repairing the moon for.
After imagined ninety years, Anya remembers Mara teaching that a clock serves the person waiting.
She abandons a perfect equation and carries the raven core out with one second remaining.
Back in normal time, Anya looks thirteen but grieves a lifetime nobody else experienced.
She discovers the century taught her how to free Elara—and that the method will destroy Pip's species.

episodes.title: The Perfect Repair Was Cruel
episodes.logline: Anya rejects the only proven solution because it would consume every clockwork key.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya destroys the old Moon Winder formula and commits to designing a new system.
episodes.location: Moon Engine calculation hall
beats: Anya presents the century formula: eight keys can replace Elara and Selene permanently.
Pip and the recovered raven both volunteer before understanding that replacement means dissolution.
Elara calls the formula correct, while Rian calls it the same injustice in cleaner language.
Anya realizes mastery made the sacrifice feel inevitable because the old designers assumed constructs were property.
She burns the formula in lunar fire despite having no alternative.
Selene shares forbidden blueprints showing the Dawn once powered time voluntarily.
The prison began only after Veyra's founders broke their agreement with it.
Deep below, the Dawn speaks through Coil and asks Anya to negotiate alone.

episodes.title: The Dawn Told the Truth
episodes.logline: The Dawn reveals Veyra stole its light, but its truthful grievance does not excuse destroying descendants.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya establishes terms for a negotiation and learns Vale caused Elara's imprisonment.
episodes.location: dreaming golden chamber beneath the Moon Engine
beats: Anya enters the Dawn's dream carrying no royal seal and no repair tools.
The Dawn appears as a small child made of sunrise because it borrows the shape Anya trusts least.
It shows founders chaining its voluntary gift into a permanent engine.
Selene was created from the Dawn's own memory and installed as a lock against her will.
Vale admits through the dream that his first stolen minute prevented Elara from completing a peaceful release.
Anya offers freedom only through a process that lets present-day Veyra survive and consent.
The Dawn agrees to one lunar cycle, but demands every stolen minute returned immediately.
When Anya wakes, all thirteen black teeth are already falling from the palace into the city.

episodes.title: Thirteen Minutes Returned at Once
episodes.logline: Returned minutes unleash years of postponed consequences across Veyra.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The kingdom accepts responsibility for consequences previously frozen away.
episodes.location: Veyra during a citywide time flood
beats: Thirteen waves of silver light race through Veyra, aging frozen cracks, storms and unfinished choices at once.
The saved avalanche finally moves toward the village Vale protected years ago.
Citizens demand he steal the minute again, and Vale nearly obeys from habit.
Anya asks the village publicly whether it wants evacuation or another hidden freeze.
The villagers choose danger with preparation and open mountain tunnels together.
Orlo redirects the avalanche while Rian coordinates shelters without royal command.
Vale returns the extraction glove to Anya and accepts arrest by the market council.
The time flood reveals a fourteenth missing minute hidden inside Anya herself.

episodes.title: Anya Was Born in a Stolen Minute
episodes.logline: Anya learns Vale froze her birth to save her life, binding her heartbeat to the Moon Engine.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya accepts that removing her minute may change who she is.
episodes.location: Elara's preserved birthing room between ticks
beats: The moon-key opens a room where newborn Anya and exhausted Elara remain preserved as light.
Mara explains Anya stopped breathing, and Vale stole the first minute to give healers more time.
The repair worked, but tied every later theft to Anya's living heartbeat.
Vale did not begin from ambition; he began from terror of losing his child.
Anya refuses to let loving motives erase the people harmed afterward.
She chooses to return her birth minute even if her memories or body change.
Pip synchronizes with her heart while Mara and Vale release the preserved room together.
Anya survives, but can no longer hear the Moon Engine's gears.

episodes.title: The Clockmaker Went Silent
episodes.logline: Without her gift, Anya must lead repairs by trusting skills and people she once treated as extensions of herself.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya becomes a collaborative leader rather than the sole chosen repairer.
episodes.location: failing lunar bridge above Veyra
beats: Anya places her hearing lens against the lunar bridge and hears only ordinary wind.
A fractured gear path requires timing she previously sensed instinctively.
She hides her silence and gives Pip an incorrect command that nearly knocks Orlo from the sky.
Rian confronts her for turning fear into secrecy just like Vale.
Anya admits the gift is gone and asks each companion what they can perceive.
Lunar vibration reaches Pip, star alignment reaches Rian, and prison strain reaches Selene.
Anya combines their reports into a repair none could perform alone.
The bridge locks safely, but Coil has occupied the final socket and refuses to move.

episodes.title: Coil Refused the Final Socket
episodes.logline: Anya must respect Coil's refusal even as the moon descends toward the city.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The repair design changes from compulsory eight-key operation to voluntary rotating stewardship.
episodes.location: final key socket on the Moon Engine rim
beats: Coil wraps around the final socket while the moon's lowest ring scrapes the mountain clouds.
Pip argues that one forced connection could save millions and be removed afterward.
Anya recognizes the logic that created Selene's prison and refuses to repeat it.
She asks Coil what condition would make participation freely reversible.
Coil demands that no key remain connected longer than one minute and every key retain an exit path.
Anya redesigns the socket as a rotating relay instead of a permanent lock.
Coil enters for one minute by choice, stabilizing the moon without surrendering his body.
The Dawn rejects the compromise and begins cracking Selene open from inside.

episodes.title: Selene Began to Break
episodes.logline: Freeing Selene releases dangerous light, forcing her to decide what parts of the Dawn she wants to remain.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Selene separates from the prison while keeping her chosen identity.
episodes.location: Selene's heart chamber
beats: Golden fractures spread across Selene's moon-pale skin as the Dawn reclaims its stolen memory.
Elara warns that separating them may erase Selene, who was formed from that memory.
Selene refuses both permanent imprisonment and being absorbed without consent.
Anya uses the rotating key relay to give Selene one free second between every shared heartbeat.
During those seconds, Selene names memories she created herself rather than inherited from the Dawn.
Pip stores those chosen memories in independent gears around her robe.
Selene steps out of the lock as a mortal child while the Dawn retains its original light.
Without a living lock, the Moon Engine opens completely over sleeping Veyra.

episodes.title: The Moon Opened Like a Door
episodes.logline: The open engine reveals the original agreement Veyra must renew—or reject forever.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Veyra's citizens gain direct knowledge of the bargain sustaining their time.
episodes.location: open Moon Engine visible above every district
beats: The moon unfolds into enormous silver rings visible from every street and village.
Words are unnecessary as the original agreement appears as shared memory across Veyra.
The Dawn once powered time in exchange for one freely given human story each generation.
Founders converted the gift into machinery because they feared an unpredictable partner.
Rian convenes open district circles instead of making a royal decision.
Some citizens prefer a mechanical moon; others accept dependence on a living being.
Anya argues the choice must include the Dawn, Selene and every clockwork key—not only humans.
Before the vote completes, Vale escapes custody and climbs toward the central winding bridge.

episodes.title: Vale Tried to Take the Burden
episodes.logline: Vale attempts to imprison himself as the new Winder, mistaking punishment for repair.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Vale abandons unilateral sacrifice and submits to shared accountability.
episodes.location: central winding bridge inside the open moon
beats: Vale chains himself to the winding bridge and orders Anya to seal the engine around him.
He believes endless labor is the only punishment large enough for what he did.
Elara says his sacrifice would again force everyone to live inside his private decision.
Anya refuses to forgive him on command or use his suffering as a repair part.
Vale unlocks one chain, then asks the public council what accountability requires.
They order him to live, testify, rebuild harmed villages and surrender royal power.
He accepts the harder future and leaves the bridge under his own strength.
The Dawn announces it will depart at sunrise unless one true story is freely offered.

episodes.title: The Kingdom Owed One Story
episodes.logline: Competing stories expose who still believes they own the moon's bargain.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya refuses to become the permanent heroic storyteller and creates a rotating civic ritual.
episodes.location: Veyra central square beneath the open moon
beats: Thousands gather to offer heroic legends, royal histories and carefully polished family memories.
The Dawn rejects each story because it was offered to control the result, not to be known.
Rian offers the shameful history of his family's theft, but the crowd has already authorized him to speak it.
Mara tells how she hid Anya and helped silence villages, without asking that the confession erase her guilt.
The Dawn listens, yet says one person's truth cannot bind future generations.
Anya proposes a rotating yearly gathering where anyone—including keys and the Dawn—may refuse.
The citizens accept an agreement that must be renewed instead of inherited automatically.
The Dawn asks Anya for the first story, and she realizes her century in the glass desert remains untold.

episodes.title: Anya Gave Away a Century
episodes.logline: Anya shares the lonely century she lived inside one minute and finally lets others understand its cost.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Anya releases her isolated mastery and the new agreement begins.
episodes.location: central square transformed by Anya's century-memory
beats: Anya tells the crowd she lived ninety imagined years while only one second passed for them.
The square becomes her empty glass workshop as the Dawn lets everyone witness without taking the memory.
They see Anya grow brilliant, cold and terrified that nobody would know the person she became.
Pip admits he remembered every version of her but stayed silent because she asked him to.
Anya releases him from that promise and apologizes for making secrecy proof of loyalty.
The Dawn accepts the story because it is offered as relationship, not payment.
Golden light enters the rotating relay and the moon begins closing around a freely renewed engine.
One damaged ring remains outside, falling directly toward Orlo and the city.

episodes.title: They Wound the Moon Together
episodes.logline: Every character contributes one reversible choice to complete the new Moon Engine.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The moon runs through shared, renewable consent; Elara returns, Selene is free, royal rule ends and Anya opens a public clock school.
episodes.location: sky above Veyra during the repaired moonrise
beats: Orlo catches the falling ring, but its weight drags him toward the mountain roofs.
Pip and the other keys rotate through sockets for one chosen minute each.
Rian coordinates citizens turning thousands of ordinary clocks to share the load without a crown.
Mara installs her repaired brass hand as a temporary counterweight, then removes it safely.
Selene guides the Dawn's light while Elara steps off the endless winding bridge at last.
Vale works beside villagers under council instruction, contributing skill without command.
Anya aligns the final gear using everyone's signals, not a special gift, and the moon turns cleanly.
Months later her public clock school closes at midnight; every clock advances one honest minute and nothing is stolen.
